verdicts.claim: A checkpoint moves WAL content back into the database file. The WAL is rewound to its start only after every frame is transferred
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'if the entire WAL has been transferred into the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then the writer will rewind the WAL back to the beginning'

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpointing is enabled by default. It runs a PASSIVE checkpoint when the WAL is N pages or longer, with N = 1000 unless SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'All automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE. Autocheckpointing is enabled by default with an interval of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT'; zero or negative turns it off

verdicts.claim: A PASSIVE checkpoint copies as many frames as it can without waiting for readers or writers. It may stop early, and it never invokes the busy handler
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode... passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished'

verdicts.claim: FULL blocks until no writer is active, then checkpoints all frames and syncs the database. RESTART does the same and then waits for readers
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2 describes FULL, RESTART ('next writer will restart the log file from the beginning') and TRUNCATE ('truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return')

verdicts.claim: The wal_checkpoint pragma returns three columns. The first is 1 when a RESTART, FULL or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked. Both counts are -1
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: three integer columns, first '1 if a RESTART or FULL or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked', second/third '-1 if there is no write-ahead log'; v2 page: after TRUNCATE 'both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero'

verdicts.claim: Litestream takes over checkpointing. It starts a long-running read transaction so no other process can checkpoint or restart the WAL
verdicts.evidence: how-it-works: 'It starts a long-running read transaction to prevent any other process from checkpointing and restarting the WAL file... manually calls out to SQLite to perform checkpoints'

verdicts.claim: Litestream runs three checkpoint tiers after each sync. A regular PASSIVE checkpoint runs at 1,000 pages (about 4 MB). Emergency tier at 121,359 pages
verdicts.evidence: guide: 'three complementary checkpoint mechanisms, evaluated in this order after each sync'; 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB'; 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000 # Default: ~4MB'; 'checkpoint-interval: 1m'; 'Only runs if WAL has at least 1 page'; passive-first fallback to TRUNCATE

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint stops at the end mark of the oldest active reader. A long-running read transaction therefore prevents the checkpointer from making progress
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress'; 'there is always at least one active reader... the WAL file will grow without bound'

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE checkpoints block writes until all read transactions finish. Long-lived readers therefore cause write outages.
verdicts.evidence: Litestream guide: 'TRUNCATE checkpoints will block writes until all read transactions complete. Long-lived readers cause extended write outages.'

verdicts.claim: By default a checkpoint does not truncate the WAL file. SQLite reuses the file and overwrites it from the start. The file shrinks only when
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning'; v2 page covers TRUNCATE
